title: Wicker application manifest (wicker-app/v1)
description: A packaged Canasta wiki application: extensions, skins, per-service image overlays, sidecars, settings, starter content, and post-install maintenance, deployed by Wicker.

wikis.description: The wikis in this instance (required, at least one). The first entry is the primary wiki: its id names the instance and it is created at the domain root. List more entries to build a wiki farm; each is added to the farm. Domains are supplied at deploy time via `-n/--domain-name` (one per wiki, matching this list's order and count), not declared here. Ordering matters — the first wiki is where `content.uploads` top-level files land.

publicAssets.description: Directory (relative to the manifest) whose contents are copied into the instance's public_assets/, served as static files (logos, favicons, robots.txt, …). The tree is copied verbatim, so per-wiki assets go under a public_assets/<wiki>/ subdirectory. Compose-only for now.

extensions.description: Every extension the app uses, bundled and custom together. An entry with no `source`/`git` is a Canasta-bundled extension (the app's settings fragment is expected to load it). An entry with `source` (local path) or `git` (URL) is a custom extension Wicker installs into the instance.

skins.description: Every skin the app uses, bundled and custom together. An entry with no `source`/`git` is a Canasta-bundled skin (the app's settings fragment is expected to load it). An entry with `source` (local path) or `git` (URL) is a custom skin Wicker installs into the instance.

images.description: Per-service derived images for the services Canasta can point at a custom image: web and elasticsearch. Each value is a Dockerfile that derives a custom image for that service from the stock image — e.g. OS packages or php.ini settings for web, an analysis plugin or alternate collation for elasticsearch. Additional containers belong in sidecars.

env.description: Plain configuration values written to the instance .env. The web pod's environment is a curated allowlist on both orchestrators, so these do NOT reach MediaWiki via getenv() — Wicker bridges declared secrets to the web tier separately; use settings fragments for app config.

secrets.description: Secrets the app needs at deploy time. Each is declared here (name + where the value goes); the VALUE is supplied via `wicker deploy --secret KEY=VALUE` (or the deploy environment), delivered per target (Compose: instance .env; Kubernetes: the per-instance Secret), and never stored in the manifest. A `sidecar:<name>` target delivers the value to that sidecar and withholds it from the web tier (envPrivate); `web` re-exports it to the MediaWiki getenv(); `env` keeps it in the .env only.

migrations.description: Versioned upgrade migrations for USER content (pages the app did not ship; shipped pages are reconciled separately). `wicker upgrade` runs every entry with installed-version < to <= manifest version, in ascending `to` order — cumulative, so 1.0->3.0 runs the 2.0 steps then the 3.0 steps.

secretTarget.description: Where a secret value is delivered: 'web', 'env', or 'sidecar:<name>'.

name.description: Env-var-style key. The value is supplied at deploy time, not here.

required.description: When true (default), deploy fails fast if no value is provided.

target.description: Where the value goes. Scalar or list of: 'web' (MediaWiki getenv()), 'env' (instance .env only), 'sidecar:<name>' (referenced by that sidecar, withheld from the web tier).

component.description: A MediaWiki extension or skin. Name-only is a Canasta-bundled component the settings fragment loads; `source` (local path) or `git` (URL) is a custom component Wicker installs into the instance.

source.description: Local path (relative to the manifest) to a custom extension/skin; copied into the instance.

git.description: Git URL for a custom extension/skin; cloned into the instance.

ref.description: Git branch, tag, or commit to check out (git sources). A branch or tag is cloned shallow; a commit SHA is checked out after a clone (full by default, bounded by `depth` if set).

depth.description: Optional shallow-clone depth (git sources; default 1 for a branch/tag `ref`). For a commit `ref`, bounds the fallback clone — the commit must be within `depth` of the default branch tip.

optional.description: The app works without this component but degrades. Documentation only.

dockerfile.description: Dockerfile path relative to the manifest. It should `FROM` the stock Canasta image for this service.

tag.description: Image tag (default derived from app name + service + version).

baseImage.description: Override the base this image derives from, forwarded as --build-arg BASE_IMAGE=... (the Dockerfile must use ARG BASE_IMAGE). For the web service, the --base-image CLI flag takes precedence. Use to build against a custom/unreleased Canasta image.

build.description: Docker build context, relative to the manifest.

dockerfile.description: Ignored: canasta builds <build>/Dockerfile. Present for forward compatibility only.

image.description: Image reference for a pull-based sidecar. Ignored when `build` is present — canasta builds and tags the context itself.

envPrivate.description: Env keys delivered to this sidecar but withheld from the web-tier getenv() bridge (for a secret only the sidecar should hold). Each must be a key in `env`. Usually set for you when a `secrets` entry targets this sidecar.

envSecret.description: Env keys sourced from the per-instance k8s app Secret (rendered as secretKeyRef instead of a cleartext value); the Compose renderer ignores this. Usually set for you on a k8s deploy when a `secrets` entry targets this sidecar.

secrets.description: Not in the canasta sidecar primitive's v1 scope — warned and dropped at deploy. Declare app secrets in the top-level `secrets:` section instead.

depends_on.description: Names of sidecar services this one starts after (start ordering on Compose; carried but not enforced on k8s — use a healthcheck for readiness).

files.description: Small config files mounted into the sidecar. `source` is a path relative to the manifest; Wicker stages it into the instance and Canasta mounts it at `mountPath` (a bind mount on Compose, a ConfigMap on k8s).

source.description: File path relative to the manifest.

ports.description: Container ports exposed on the instance network (reachable by service name, e.g. redis:6379). Internal only — not published to the host.

volumes.description: Mounted volumes. `persistent: true` -> a named volume (Compose) / ReadWriteOnce PVC (k8s); otherwise ephemeral.

sysctls.description: Kernel sysctls the container needs (e.g. vm.max_map_count for Elasticsearch). Not in the canasta sidecar primitive's v1 scope — warned and dropped at deploy.

healthcheck.description: One of: `command` (exec), `tcp` (port check), or `path`+`port` (HTTP GET). `port` alone is a TCP check.

path.description: Source path relative to the manifest.

install.description: Destination relative to the instance directory, e.g. config/settings/global/Settings.php.

vars.description: When present, the file is treated as a template and these {{KEY}} placeholders are substituted (values may reference deploy-time --var). When absent, the file is copied verbatim.

wiki.description: One wiki in the instance. The first wiki in `wikis` is the primary (created with the instance at the domain root); the rest build a wiki farm. Domains are NOT declared here — they are supplied at deploy time via `-n/--domain-name` (one per wiki, in this order), since a shipped manifest has no reasonable default domain.

uploads.description: Media files uploaded into the wikis at deploy time via importImages.php. Files directly in `dir` are uploaded to the first wiki; files in a `dir/<wiki-id>/` subdirectory are uploaded to that wiki. Compose-only for now.

dir.description: Directory holding the media files, relative to the manifest (default ./content/uploads).

pages.description: Starter wiki pages imported directly from local files. Each page's file path is derived from its title, mirroring the wiki namespace as a directory: the namespace ':' becomes a '/' (so 'Template:Expense' is 'Template/Expense.mediawiki'), spaces and subpage '/' are kept, and a main-namespace page sits at the root; '.mediawiki' is appended unless the title ends in .css/.js. Override per page with `file`.

dir.description: Directory holding the page files, relative to the manifest.

oneOf.description: Full page title, e.g. "Template:Expense" or "Main Page"; filename derived.

file.description: Explicit file (relative to `dir`, or to the manifest if no `dir`), overriding the derived name.

to.description: The app version these steps migrate TO. Must be unique across entries and not exceed the manifest version.

migration.description: template-calls steps are idempotent; action steps (maintenance/shell/page-edit) re-run wholesale if an upgrade is retried after a failure — write them to be safe to repeat.

templateCallsStep.description: Rewrite every call of a template across the wiki's user pages (shipped pages are excluded — reconciliation already delivered their new text). Calls via the template's Template-namespace redirects are matched too. Deterministic, parser-based (mwparserfromhell); pages whose wikitext cannot be safely rewritten are reported, never guessed.

template.description: Template name, without the Template: prefix.

templateTransform.description: One deterministic edit to a template call's NAMED parameters, applied to every matched invocation.

oneOf.description: Rename a parameter, value untouched. A call already using the new name (or lacking the old one) is left alone.
Add a parameter with a literal `value`, or copy it `from` another parameter (skipped if the source is absent). With ifAbsent (default true) an existing value is never clobbered.
Remove a parameter AND ITS VALUE — an explicit data-loss decision.
Rewrite a parameter's value by exact (whitespace-trimmed) lookup. Values not in the map are kept; with unmapped: report (default) they are also listed in the upgrade report for a human.

action.description: A named post-install / lifecycle action. Deliberately generic — no app-domain knowledge.

oneOf.description: Run a maintenance script. With `extension`, the script is resolved under that extension's maintenance/ dir; without, under core maintenance/.

source.description: Path to wikitext (relative to the manifest) or literal content.
